title: French Onion Soup - Light
text: French Onion Soup - Light French Onion Soup – Light Double Recipe (Jan 2020 Adjustments) + Single Recipe Reference Ingredients – Double Recipe (Used Version) 2 tbsp EVOO 4 large onions, halved and thinly sliced 1 clove garlic Kosher salt Large bundle bouquet garni (fresh thyme + fresh bay leaves) 1/2 cup strong dry white wine 1/2 cup strong bourbon (Jim Beam) 2 tbsp soy sauce 12 cups beef broth 8 slices baguette (1/2-inch thick) 1/2 cup freshly grated Gruyère cheese Ingredients – Single Recipe (Reference) 1 tbsp EVOO 2 large onions, halved and thinly sliced Kosher salt 1/4 cup dry white wine 1 tbsp soy sauce 6 cups beef broth Four 1/2-inch-thick slices whole-grain baguette 1/4 cup freshly grated Gruyère cheese Instructions (Jan 2020 Adjustments) In a large enameled cast-iron casserole, heat the oil until shimmering. Add the onions and garlic and cook over moderate heat, stirring occasionally, until onions wilt and begin to brown (about 7 min). Add a generous pinch of salt and cook over moderately low heat, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and golden, 25–30 minutes. Add wine, bourbon (or cognac), and soy sauce. Cook over moderate heat, scraping up browned bits, until evaporated (about 3 minutes). Add beef stock and bouquet garni. Bring to a boil, then simmer over moderately low heat until well flavored and slightly reduced (about 10 minutes). Taste — do not add salt ; it’s salty enough. Preheat broiler. Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet and top each with 1 tbsp Gruyère. Broil 6 inches from heat until cheese melts and begins to brown (about 2 minutes). Ladle soup into bowls and top with cheese toasts. Make Ahead Soup can be made through Step 2 and refrigerated for up to 2 days. Reheat gently before serving. Notes One serving: 145 cal, 6g fat, 1.6g sat fat, 14g carbs, 2g fiber, 8g protein.

title: French-Inspired Potato Salad
text: French-Inspired Potato Salad French Potato Salad Ingredients: Delete All 2 pounds small red or Yukon gold potatoes (no larger than 2-inches in diameter) 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon kosher salt, divided 1/2 cup loosely packed fresh tender herbs, such as parsley, basil, dill, tarragon, or a combination 4 medium scallions 1/3 cup olive oil 1/4 cup red wine vinegar 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard 1 tablespoon whole-grain Dijon mustard (or additional 1 tablespoon regular Dijon) 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper Instructions: Place 2 pounds small red or Yukon gold potatoes and 1 tablespoon of the kosher salt in a large saucepan. Cover by 1 inch with cool water, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer until the potatoes are easily pierced with a knife, 15 to 20 minutes. Meanwhile, chop the herbs and scallions, and make the dressing. Coarsely chop 1/2 cup loosely packed fresh tender herbs. Thinly slice 4 medium scallions. Place 1/3 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon whole-grain Dijon mustard, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and the remaining 1 teaspoon kosher salt in a large bowl. Whisk well to combine and emulsify. Drain the cooked potatoes in a colander and rinse under cold water just until they are cool enough to handle but still warm. Halve the potatoes (or quarter if large) and transfer to the bowl of vinaigrette. Gently toss to coat the potatoes. Add the herbs and scallions and toss lightly to combine. Set aside for 10 minutes to allow for the flavors to meld. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Fresh String Green Beans Recipe
text: Fresh String Green Beans Recipe Fresh String Green Beans Ingredients: Delete All 5 lbs green beans 3 tbsp bacon grease (adjust for fewer beans) Directions: Delete All Melt bacon grease in the bottom of a pan. Place wet, cleaned green beans in the pan. Salt and sprinkle with brown sugar. Stir until coated with grease. Add water until it surrounds the beans but doesn’t cover them. Cook on high for 15 minutes, then reduce to warm or simmer for 2–3 hours. Always check to ensure beans have water.

title: Fudge
text: Fudge Fudge Ingredients Delete All 3 Cups Granulated Sugar 3 TBS Cocoa 1 Cup Milk 1/2 tsp Cream of Tartar 1 tsp Butter 1 1/2 tsp of Vanilla Instructions Delete All Cook first three ingredients until it comes to a boil, add Tartar Boil as slowly as possible and cook until it forms a ball Remove from heat and set in pan of cold water Add butter and vanilla Do not beat until very thoroughly cold, then add nuts. --> Image - add later --> Image - add later

title: Garden Minestrone
text: Garden Minestrone Garden Minestrone Ingredients: Delete All 2 tsp EVOO 1 Cup Onion, Chopped 2 tsp Fresh Oregano, Chopped 4 Garlic Cloves, Minced 3 Cups Yellow Squash, Chopped 3 Cups Zucchini, Chopped 1 Cup Carrot, Chopped 1 Cup Fresh Corn 4 Cups Tomato, Chopped 3 - 14 oz Cans Chicken broth 1/2 Cup Pasta 1 - 15 oz can Great Northern Beans, rinsed and drained 1 - 6 oz Package Spinach 3/4 tsp Salt 1/2 tsp Freshly Ground Pepper 1 Cup Grated Asiago Cheese Coarsely Ground Pepper Instructions: Delete All Heat oil in a dutch oven over medium high heat. Add onion and saute 3 min or until softened. Add oregano and garlic, saute 1 min. Stir in squash, zucchini, carrot and corn; saute 5 min or until veggies are tender. Remove from heat. Place 3 Cups tomato and 1 can broth in blender; process until smooth. Add tomato mixture to pan; return pan to heat. Stir in remaining 1 Cup tomato and remaining 2 cans broth; bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 20 min. Add pasta and beans to pan; cook 10 min or until pasta is tender, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat. Stir in Spinach, salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Ladle soup into individual bowls; top with cheese. Garnish with coarsely ground black pepper.

title: Garden Vegetable Grilled Pizza
text: Garden Vegetable Grilled Pizza Garden Vegetable Grilled Pizza Ingredients: Delete All 1 1/2 cups fresh baby spinach 1 tsp olive oil 1 recipe Homemade pizza crust OR Boboli bread 6 Tbs grated Parmesan cheese 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced 1 1/2 cups chunky tomato sauce 12 oz bite-size fresh mozzarella cheese balls, drained, thinly sliced, and patted dry 1 1/2 cups grilled corn kernels 1 1/2 cups grilled eggplant 6 slices of bacon, crisp cooked, crumbled 1 1/2 lb assorted heirloom tomatoes, cut up small fresh basil leaves Ground Pepper Sea Salt Directions: Delete All 1. In a small bowl combine spinach, 1 tsp oil and a dash of salt. 2. Using Boboli crust, brush with olive oil and grill on both sides for 2 min. 3. Sprinkle 1 Tbs of Parmesan cheese and one clove garlic over crust; top with 1/4 cup of tomato sauce. Add 1/4 cup of spinach mixture, 2 oz of the mozzarella cheese, 1/4 cup of corn, 1/4 cup of eggplant and 1 slice of the crumbled bacon. Grill pizza 3 to 5 min more or until crust is crisp and cheese is melted. 4. Before serving, top pizzas with tomato, basil, and pepper (Optional sea salt).

title: Harissa Chicken Skewers - Blue Apron
text: Harissa Chicken Skewers - Blue Apron Harissa Chicken Skewers - Blue Apron Ingredients Delete All Makes: 2 Servings Prep Time: 10 Min. Cook Time: 35 - 45 min 2 Boneless, Skinless Chicken Breasts 8 Wooden Skewers 3 oz Semi-Pearled Khorasan Wheat 2 Cloves Garlic 1 Persimmon 1/2 Bunch Kale 2 Tbs Red Wine Vinegar 1 Tbs Red Harissa Paste 1/4 Cup Labneh Cheese Instructions Delete All Cook the Khorasan Wheat: Heat a medium pot of salted water to boiling on high. Once boiling, add the Khorasan wheat and cook, uncovered, 16 - 18 min, or until tender. Drain thoroughly and set aside in a warm place. Prepare the Ingredients: Peel and mince the garlic. Remove and discard the kale stems; roughly chop the leaves. Core and small dice the persimmon. Cut each chicken breast lengthwise into 4 equal-sized strips; transfer to a medium bowl. Assemble the Chicken Skewers: To the bowl of chicken strips add: 1/4 of the labneh, as much of the harissa paste as you'd like, season with salt and pepper. Toss to thoroughly coat. Thread the seasoned chicken lengthwise onto the skewers. Transfer onto a plate. Cook The Chicken Skewers: In a large (nonstick) heat 1 Tbs of olive oil on medium-high until hot. Add the chicken skewers and cook 3 - 4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked through. Leave the pan..... Make the Khorasan Wheat salad: Add 1 Tbs of olive oil to the pan of reserved fond and heat on medium-high until hot. Add the garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the kale; season with salt and pepper. Cook stirring occasionally, 30 seconds to 1 min, or until slightly wilted. Add the vinegar and 1/2 cup water (be careful the water may splatter) Cook, stirring occasionally 4 - 5 min, or until the kale has wilted and most of the liquid has cooked off. Add the persimmon and cooked khorasan wheat. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1 - 2 min. or until thoroughly combined and the persimmon is slightly softened. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Season the Labneh and Plate your Dish: Place the remaining labneh in a bowl; season with salt and pepper. Stir to incorporate. Divide the salad and chicken and serve with the labneh on the side (and remaining harissa paste). Image - add later --> Image - add later -->

title: Italian Wedding Soup
text: Italian Wedding Soup Italian Wedding Soup Ingredients Delete All Meatballs ** Last time I doubled the meatball ingredients and froze half of them ** 8 oz lean ground beef 8 oz ground pork 1/2 cup fresh hearty white bread crumbs* 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley 1 1/2 tsp minced fresh oregano 1/2 cup finely shredded parmesan 1 large egg Salt and freshly ground black pepper 1 Tbsp olive oil Soup 1 Tbsp olive oil 1 1/4 cups 1/4-inch diced carrots 1 1/4 cups diced yellow onion 3/4 cup 1/4-inch diced celery 4 cloves garlic , minced (1 1/2 Tbsp) 5 (14.5 oz) cans low-sodium chicken broth 1 cup dry acini de pepe or orzo pasta** 6 oz fresh spinach , chopped Finely shredded parmesan , for serving Instructions Delete All For the meatballs: Add beef and pork to a large mixing bowl. Add in bread crumbs, parsley, oregano, parmesan, egg, 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Gently toss and break up mixture with hands to evenly coat and distribute. Shape mixture into very small meatballs, about 3/4 inch to 1 inch and transfer to a large plate. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add half of the meatballs and cook until browned, turning occasionally (to brown on 2 or 3 sides), about 4 minutes total. Transfer meatballs to a plate lined with paper towels while leaving oil in skillet. Repeat process with remaining meatballs (note that meatballs won't be cooked through at this point, they'll continue to cook through in the soup). For the soup: While meatballs are browning, heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add carrots, onions and celery and saute until veggies have softened about 6 - 8 minutes, add garlic and saute 1 minute longer. Pour in chicken broth, season soup with salt and pepper to taste and bring mixture to a boil. Add in pasta and meatballs, reduce heat to light boil (about medium or medium-low). Cover and cook, stirring occasionally until pasta is tender and meatballs have cooked through, about 10 minutes, while adding in spinach during the last minute of cooking. Serve warm, sprinkle each serving with parmesan cheese. Notes *I recommend using bread such as a La Brea french loaf. Just grind up a slice in a food processor to find crumbs. Save the remaining bread for serving (slathered with butter of course) or freeze for another later use. **If you like a more brothier soup you can reduce pasta to 3/4 cup. Note that as the soup sits the pasta will absorb more broth so you can add more broth to thin the soup as desired. Image - add later --> Image - add later -->

title: Marinated Strip Steaks with Gorgonzola Sauce
text: Marinated Strip Steaks with Gorgonzola Sauce Marinated Strip Steaks With Gorgonzola Sauce · Serves 4 Ingredients Delete All Marinade 2 cups beef broth 1 cup dry red wine 1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped 2 tbsp tomato paste Steaks 4 New York strip steaks Extra-virgin olive oil Kosher salt Freshly ground black pepper Gorgonzola Sauce 1 tbsp unsalted butter 2 tbsp minced shallot 1 cup sour cream 4 oz crumbled gorgonzola cheese (about 1 cup) Instructions In a large glass baking dish, whisk together beef broth, red wine, onion, and tomato paste until smooth. Lightly brush steaks with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and let rest at room temperature for 15–30 minutes. Meanwhile, melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot and cook until tender, about 2 minutes. Stir in sour cream and gorgonzola; cook until the sauce begins to simmer and cheese is melted, about 3 minutes. Remove sauce from heat, add ¼ tsp black pepper, cover, and keep warm. Grill steaks to desired doneness. Rest briefly, then serve topped with warm gorgonzola sauce.

title: Meatball Stroganoff
text: Meatball Stroganoff Meatball Stroganoff Comfort-food classic with a creamy beefy sauce Ingredients Delete All 3 cups egg noodles 1 tbsp olive oil 1 package (12 oz) frozen meatballs or 1 lb fresh meatballs 1 1/2 cups beef broth 1 tsp dried parsley flakes 1/4 tsp dried basil 1/4 tsp dried oregano 1/4 tsp salt 1/4 tsp black pepper 1 cup heavy whipping cream 3/4 cup sour cream Instructions Cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente; drain and set aside. In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs, then remove from the pan. Add beef broth to the skillet, stirring to loosen browned bits from the bottom. Add parsley, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil and cook 5–7 minutes, until liquid reduces to about 1/2 cup. Return meatballs to the pan. Add cooked noodles and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 3–5 minutes until slightly thickened. Stir in sour cream and heat through. Do not boil after adding sour cream. text: Minestrone Soup Minestrone Soup Ingredients Delete All Olive Oil and Butter (the substitute was fine) 1 Small Onion, Diced 1 Cup Carrots, Chopped 1 Cup Celery, Chopped 4 - 6 Garlic Cloves, minced 5 oz Green Beans trimmed into 1" pieces 1 Zucchini, quartered and thickly sliced 2 - 14.5 oz cans Hunts Fire Roasted Tomatoes, diced with juices 1 - 15 oz can Tomato Sauce 1 - 15.5 oz can Kidney Beans, drained and rinsed 1 1/2 tsp EACH Dried Basil, Dried Parsley 1 tsp EACH Dried Oregano, salt, sugar 1/2 tsp EACH Black Pepper, Dried Thyme 1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes 1 Bay Leaf 6 Cups Low Sodium Chicken Broth 2 Cups Water Add Later 1 1/2 Cups Small Pasta Shells (Used whole wheat bow ties) 2 - 3 Cups Baby Spinach (EXCHANGE KALE) Freshly Grated Parmesan Fresh Basil (Optional) Instructions Delete All Melt butter in olive oil in large Dutch oven / soup pot. Add onions, carrots, and celery. Cook, stirring often, for 5 - 7 min or until the onions are translucent. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add all remaining ingredients through the water. Cover soup and bring to a boil. Uncover and reduce to a gentle simmer for 10 min. Do NOT add pasta if will be freezing later. Cook separately and add as used. Remove from heat and stir in spinach. Let wilt, about 1 min. Add water for a less Chunky soup. Garnish with grated Parmesan. Recipe Notes Correct Pasta: My favorite pasta to use for this Minestrone Soup recipe is small/mini pasta shells. Small pasta shapes that are about the size of your chopped veggies ensure you get the right ratio of pasta to veggies in every slurpful. Other small pastas such as ditalini (the small short tubes) and mini penne will also work. I don't recommend medium pastas. Al Dente Pasta : Cook the pasta just until al dente (meaning it has a little bite) to it because it will still cook a little once you remove it from the heat and nothing is worse than ruining a whole pot of Minestrone Soup than with soggy pasta. Cook Pasta Separately: As this Minestrone Soup Recipe is written, the pasta cooks in the pot with the veggies. If you aren't prepared to babysit your pasta towards the end of cooking, then simply cook your pasta separately and add to individual bowls. You will also want to cook your pasta separately if you plan on freezing your Minestrone Soup. Customize Veggies: This Minestrone Recipe is very forgiving when it comes to customizing the veggies with whatever you have on hand. You can swap the spinach for Swiss chard or baby kale, add potatoes (chopped ½" and add with green beans), add frozen peas, cabbage (both at end when you would add spinach), etc. Zucchini: The zucchini takes the least amount of time to cook, so take care you cut it on the thick side – at least ¼" chunks. Green Beans: I like fresh green beans but they are not my favorite vegetable – but guess what?! They are my favorite vegetable in this Minestrone Soup Recipe – I highly recommend them! Add protein. I love this Minestrone Soup as the base for whatever meat we have on ha

title: Monkfish with Curried Mussels
text: Monkfish with Curried Mussels Monkfish with Curried Mussels Serves 2–4 Ingredients Delete All 1 large monkfish tail, filleted in two 1/2 lb mussels, cleaned and beard removed 2 sprigs thyme 2 bay leaves 1/2 cup dry white wine (or as needed) 1 carrot, peeled and sliced 1 small leek, sliced 1 small celery stalk, sliced 1 clove garlic, minced 1 tsp curry powder 2 pinches turmeric powder 1 tbsp curry powder + 1 tbsp salt (for dusting fish) 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream Handful of cilantro, chopped Butter Olive oil *Ask the fishmonger to remove gray membrane* Instructions Clean monkfish fillets and cut each in half. Dust with curry/salt mix and set aside 5 minutes. Heat a wide pan until hot; add thyme, bay leaves, and mussels. Add wine, cover immediately, and cook ~30 seconds until mussels open. Strain off & reserve juices; remove mussels from shells and set aside. Sauté carrot, leek, celery, garlic with 1 tsp curry powder, turmeric, and thyme until soft. Strain in mussel juices; reduce. Pat monkfish dry and pan-fry in hot olive oil until golden (3–4 minutes). Add mussels to vegetables; warm through. Add cream and bring to a boil; mix in cilantro. Divide mussel mixture into warm bowls; slice monkfish thickly and place on top.

text: One - Pan Chicken w/ Lima Beans, Leeks, Spinach One - Pan Chicken w/ Lima Beans, Leeks, Spinach Ingredients Delete All 1 Whole chicken cut up, skin removed 1 TBS Olive oil 1 Head Garlic, cut in half horizontally 1 Leek, trimmed, halved lengthwise, and sliced 3/4 Cup dry white wine 1 1/2 Cups low sodium chicken broth 2 Thyme sprigs 2 - 15 oz cans lima beans, drained and rinsed (can sub. Brown the chicken on all sides until nicely colored. Add the garlic, cut side down, then add the leak slices and stir around in the oil. Notes ** This recipe can be halved ** ** If you want to leave the skin on: Turn chicken skin side up after browning and be careful not to pour the wine or the stock over the browned skin because it won't crisp up properly in the oven. ** ** Per Serving: Calories 509 Fat 16.0 Saturated Fat 4.0 Carbs 18.0 Sugar 2.0 Fiber 10.0 Protein 58.0 Sodium .62 Image - add later --> Image - add later -->

title: Panfried Sea Bass (Halibut) and Scallops with Sauce Beurre Blanc
text: Panfried Sea Bass (Halibut) and Scallops with Sauce Beurre Blanc Panfried Sea Bass (Halibut) and Scallops with Sauce Beurre Blanc Prep: 15 min | Cook: 25 min | Servings: 2 Ingredients Delete All Sauce 1 TBS very finely chopped shallot 2 TBS white wine vinegar 2 TBS dry white wine 2 TBS water 1/4 lb (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, diced Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste Fish & Scallops 2 Sea Bass fillets, scaled, rinsed, and drained (or halibut) Salt and freshly ground black pepper 2 TBS butter 1 TBS olive oil 6 scallops Instructions To make the sauce, place shallot, vinegar, wine, and water into a small heavy-based pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until ~1 TBS of syrupy liquid remains. Reduce heat to lowest setting and whisk in butter one piece at a time. The sauce should be pale and custard-like. Season with salt and pepper. Meanwhile, season fish and scallops with salt and pepper. Heat half of the remaining butter and oil in a heavy-based frying pan. Add fish skin-side down. Press with spatula to prevent curling. Cook 2–3 min until skin is crispy and flesh turns opaque, leaving a thin pink strip in center. Carefully turn fish and cook 1–2 more minutes until done. In another small frying pan, heat remaining butter and oil. Add scallops and cook 4–5 min, turning once. Spoon sauce beurre blanc onto warmed plates, arrange sugar peas, set fish fillet on top, garnish with scallops, and serve immediately. Tips for Perfect Sauce Beurre Blanc Use cold butter straight from the fridge and cut into small cubes for smooth emulsification. Whisk constantly and add butter gradually to prevent the sauce from separating. Keep the heat very low once you start adding butter; too much heat will cause the sauce to split. If the sauce begins to separate, remove from heat and whisk in a tablespoon of cold water to bring it back together. Prepare the sauce just before serving; beurre blanc does not reheat well. For extra flavor, add a teaspoon of fresh lemon juice at the end to brighten the sauce.

title: Pappardelle al Ragu
text: Pappardelle al Ragu Pappardelle al Ragu Servings: 4–6 | Prep: 20 min | Cook: 2 hours Ingredients Delete All 2 Tbs Butter 2 Tbs Olive Oil 4 oz Pancetta, diced 1 small onion, finely chopped 1 celery stalk, finely chopped 1 carrot, finely chopped 2 garlic cloves, crushed 1 lb lean ground beef 1/2 cup beef stock (plus more if needed) 2 Tbs Tomato paste 14 oz can diced tomatoes (fire roasted optional) Salt & Pepper, to taste 1/3 cup whole milk, warmed 1 lb package of pappardelle (wide noodles) Parmesan cheese, grated to serve Instructions Melt butter with oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed saucepan. Cook pancetta 1–2 min. Add onion, celery, carrot, and garlic. Cook, stirring occasionally, 10 min until softened but not browned. Optional: Cook meat separately to drain excess fat, then stir in and cook until evenly browned (~10 min). Add stock, tomato paste, and diced tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to very low. Cover and simmer gently 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, adding more stock if necessary. Stir in warmed milk, cover, and simmer another 30 min. Cook pappardelle according to package directions. Serve with sauce and grated Parmesan. Tips for Perfect Ragu Cooking the meat separately can help reduce excess grease for a cleaner sauce. Maintain very low heat during simmering to prevent sauce from scorching. Stir occasionally to keep the ragu smooth and prevent sticking. Use whole milk for a richer finish; add gradually to avoid curdling. Fire-roasted diced tomatoes add extra depth of flavor. Resting the sauce for a few minutes before serving helps flavors meld beautifully.

title: Roasted Potato Carrot, and Broccoli Onions
text: Roasted Potato Carrot, and Broccoli Onions Roasted Potato Carrot, and Broccoli Onions Two-pan method for perfectly caramelized vegetables Ingredients Delete All Potatoes, cut into ¾–1 inch chunks or wedges Carrots, halved lengthwise if thick, cut into 2–3 inch pieces Onion, cut into large wedges Broccoli florets, stems peeled and sliced Green onions, left whole or halved (added last) Olive oil (about 1–1½ tbsp per pan) Salt Black pepper Optional: garlic powder, paprika, rosemary, thyme Instructions (Two-Pan Method) Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Use two large sheet pans to prevent overcrowding. Cut vegetables to similar thickness for even cooking. Toss each vegetable group separately with olive oil, salt, pepper, and optional seasonings. Pan 1 – Hard Vegetables Add potatoes and carrots to Pan 1 in a single layer, cut side down when possible. Roast for 20 minutes. Flip and continue roasting for 10–15 more minutes until tender and browned. Pan 2 – Medium Vegetables Add onions and broccoli to Pan 2. Roast for 12–15 minutes, stirring once halfway. Add green onions during the final 5 minutes if using. Remove pans when vegetables are caramelized and tender. Combine pans if desired, adjust seasoning, and serve. Why Two Pans Works Prevents steaming and promotes browning Allows each vegetable group to cook perfectly Easier stirring and flipping

title: Salmon with Chipotle Butter

title: Sausage Stuffed Zucchini
text: Sausage Stuffed Zucchini Sausage Stuffed Zucchini Serves 4 Puree Ingredients Delete All 4 large plum tomatoes (~1 lb total) 1 small onion, cut into 1/2 inch slices 2 small bell peppers (1 red, 1 yellow) 2 TBS fresh chopped basil & oregano leaves 2 garlic cloves 2 TBS red wine vinegar 1 tsp kosher salt 1/4 tsp black pepper 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) Zucchini & Sausage Ingredients 4 medium zucchini, cut in half lengthwise 1 lb Italian sausage, medium or sweet 1 cup grated Romano cheese 1/3 cup panko bread crumbs Instructions Grill tomatoes, onions, and peppers over direct medium heat until soft (tomatoes & onions ~8–10 min; peppers ~10–15 min). Remove vegetables as done. Cover peppers to steam for 10 min. When cool enough to handle, peel tomatoes and remove stem ends. Peel, core, and seed the peppers. In a food processor, combine tomatoes, onion, peppers, basil, oregano, garlic, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Puree until smooth, slowly adding olive oil. Warm puree in a medium pan over low heat until slightly thickened, 3–5 minutes. Remove from heat. Score zucchini where seeds meet the flesh and scoop out with a spoon. In a medium bowl, gently combine sausage, cheese, bread crumbs, and 1/2 cup of puree. Fill zucchini boats with mixture. Grill zucchini over direct medium heat about 15 min. Spread remaining puree over each zucchini after plating. Serve with rice or pasta.

title: Scallop Risotto
text: Scallop Risotto Scallop Risotto Ingredients: Delete All 6 cups fish stock (or chicken, veggie depending on main course) 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil 3 tablespoons unsalted butter 1 shallot, finely diced (1 medium shallot = 1/4 Cup) Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper 3/4 cup arborio rice 1/3 cup dry white wine 8 ounces pencil (thin) asparagus 1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan, plus more for serving Zest and juice of 1 lemon - easy on the lemon; try zest and half juice 10 sea scallops, "foot" muscles removed, scallops patted dry 2 tablespoons chopped fresh chives Instructions: Delete All - Heat the stock in a medium saucepan over medium heat; lower the heat so the stock stays warm without simmering. - Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the shallot, season with salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 1 minute. - Add the rice, season with salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the rice is coated and fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the wine and cook, stirring constantly, until completely absorbed, about 1 minute. - Ladle about 1/4 cup hot stock into the risotto and cook, stirring, until absorbed. Continue to add the stock in additions of about 1/4 cup, gradually working up to 1/2-cup additions, stirring until absorbed before adding more. Continue adding broth and stirring until the rice is tender and creamy, about 18 minutes. - While the rice cooks, trim the woody end of the asparagus off and cut the stalks into 3/4-inch pieces. - Once the rice is cooked, remove the pan from the heat and stir in the asparagus, remaining 2 tablespoons butter, the Parmesan, lemon juice and lemon zest, stirring until the risotto is creamy. Add a splash of water to loosen, if necessary. Season with salt and pepper if needed. - Heat a medium nonstick skillet over high heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Season the scallops with salt and pepper and add them to the skillet. Cook, undisturbed, until browned and crisp on the bottom, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip the scallops and continue to cook until just cooked through, about 1 more minute. Transfer to a plate. - Divide the risotto between bowls and top with the scallops; sprinkle with chives and more Parmesan.

text: Shrimp and Grits Shrimp and Grits A lighter take on a Southern classic dish. title: Shrimp Diane
text: Shrimp Diane Shrimp Diane Makes 2 Servings Ingredients: 1 3/4 lbs medium shrimp (with heads & tails if using for stock) 6 Tbs seafood stock 1 1/2 sticks unsalted butter (divided) 1/4 cup very finely chopped green onions 3/4 tsp salt 1/2 tsp minced garlic 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper 1/4 tsp white pepper 1/4 tsp black pepper 1/4 tsp dried sweet basil leaves 1/4 tsp dried thyme 1/4 tsp dried oregano 1/2 lb mushrooms, sliced 1/4" 3 Tbs finely chopped fresh parsley French bread, pasta, or hot cooked rice (for serving) Instructions: Rinse and peel shrimp; reserve shells to make shrimp stock. In a large skillet, melt 1 stick of butter over high heat. Add green onions, salt, garlic, cayenne, basil, thyme, and oregano. Stir well. title: Slow Cooker Chicken Marsala
text: Slow Cooker Chicken Marsala Slow Cooker Chicken Marsala Serves 4 Ingredients Delete All 4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs 1 cup sliced cremini mushrooms 3/4 cup Marsala wine 1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth 2 tbsp olive oil 1 small onion, finely chopped 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp cornstarch + 1 tbsp water (slurry) 1 tsp dried thyme (or fresh sprigs) Salt & pepper to taste Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish) Instructions Season chicken with salt and pepper. In a skillet over medium heat, sear chicken in olive oil until lightly golden, 2–3 minutes per side. Place chicken in slow cooker. Top with mushrooms, onion, garlic, and thyme. Pour Marsala wine and chicken broth over the chicken. Cover and cook on LOW for 5–6 hours or HIGH for 2.5–3 hours. Remove chicken. Stir cornstarch slurry into sauce and cook on HIGH for 10–15 minutes to thicken. Return chicken to slow cooker, coat with sauce, garnish with parsley, and serve warm.

text: Slow Cooker Spaghetti & Meatballs Slow Cooker Spaghetti & Meatballs Ingredients Delete All 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes 1 (15-ounce) can diced tomatoes 1 (15-ounce) can tomato sauce 1 cup beef stock 1/2 medium sweet onion, diced 3 cloves garlic, minced 2 teaspoons granulated sugar Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste 8 ounces spaghetti, broken in half 1/3 cup chopped fresh basil leaves (optional) FOR THE MEATBALLS: 1 pound lean ground beef 1/2 pound Italian sausage, casing removed 1/2 cup Panko 1/4 cup whole milk 1 large egg, lightly beaten 3 tablespoons freshly grated Parmesan 3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley leaves 2 cloves garlic, minced Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil Instructions Delete All In a large bowl, combine ground beef, sausage, Panko, milk, egg, Parmesan, parsley and garlic; season with salt and pepper, to taste. title: Smoked Beef Chuck Roast (Blade) - Texas Style
text: Smoked Beef Chuck Roast (Blade) - Texas Style Smoked Beef Chuck Roast (Blade) - Texas Style Ingredients: Delete All 3-4 pounds chuck roast 1 tablespoon coarse salt 1 tablespoon coarse ground black pepper 1 teaspoon granulated garlic 2 cups beef broth unsalted Instructions: Delete All - Remove the meat from the refrigerator and allow to sit at room temperature for 45-60 minutes. - Preheat the Smoker: Preheat your smoker to 225°F using Oak, apple, hickory or pecan. Allow to heat with the lid closed for 10-15 minutes. - Prepare the Dry Rub: combine the salt, pepper and garlic powder in a small bowl. - Season: after roast has sat for 45-60 mins at room temperature, liberally apply the dry rub to the roast, using your hands to press it in. - Smoke: place the roast on the center of the grill grate. Smoke for approximately 4 hours until the internal temperature registers 165 degrees Fahrenheit. - Prepare baking tray: pour 2 cups of beef broth into a 9×13 disposable baking tray. Once the roast registers 165 degrees, remove from the smoker, place in the tray and cover tightly with foil. - Continue Cooking: at this point, you can continue to cook on the smoker, or place in an oven preheated to 250 degrees F. If smoking, increase the smoker’s temperature to 250 degrees F. - Continue cooking the roast until the internal temperature registers 200 to 203 degrees F. Approximately another 3 hours. - Remove from the oven or the smoker keeping the roast covered. Let rest for 30 minutes before slicing. - Remove the roast from the pan and the cooking liquid. Slice the roast against the grain, and spoon over some of the liquid for serving.

title: Smoked Boneless Leg of Lamb
text: Smoked Boneless Leg of Lamb NAVIGATION GOES HERE Smoked Boneless Leg of Lamb Recipe Ingredients Lamb: 5–6 lb Boneless Lamb Leg (or two 2.5 lb legs) Olive oil, salt & pepper Fresh thyme, rosemary, garlic (minced) — reserve some for baste Veal Magic Baste: 1 cup red wine vinegar Reserved thyme, rosemary & garlic Salt & pepper 1/2 cup vegetable oil (stir in) Beet Sauce: 2 cups Greek yogurt 1/2 cup beet juice 1/2 cup chopped dill fronds 2 TBS fresh mint, finely chopped Salt & pepper Instructions The Night Before: Cover lamb with olive oil, salt & pepper Mince herbs & garlic and spread over lamb Refrigerate overnight The Day Of: Remove lamb several hours ahead to bring to room temperature Preheat smoker to 300°F using apple or cherry wood Smoke lamb at 250–275°F for 2.5 hours Baste every 45 minutes until internal temp reaches 130°F Heat grill to medium-high Reverse sear until internal temp reaches 140°F Remove from grill & rest 10–15 minutes Slice and serve immediately FOOTER GOES HERE

title: Smoked Chicken Wings
text: Smoked Chicken Wings Smoked Chicken Wings Serves 4–6 Ingredients Delete All 1 package chicken wings (Gerber Party Pack) Olive oil Poultry Magic seasoning Hickory wood chunks Instructions Prepare wings the day before cooking. Pat wings dry. Place wings in a large bowl and lightly coat with olive oil; mix to coat evenly. Sprinkle Poultry Magic seasoning over wings and mix to coat. Place wings on 2 oiled smoker racks. Refrigerate uncovered overnight. Preheat smoker to 250°F. Smoke wings at 225–250°F for 1 1/2 – 2 hours, until internal temp reaches 160°F. Remove wings and let rest at least 10 minutes before serving.

title: Smoked Duck
text: Smoked Duck Smoked Duck Ingredients: Delete All 1 5 - 6 Lb duck (purchased 3 days before to thaw in refrigerator) Apple and/or Cherry Wood Chips 1 Orange and/or mandarin oranges 1 Onion Glaze: 1 Tbs Honey 1 Tbs Molasses 2 Tbs Orange Juice 1 Tbs Balsamic Vinegar Zest of 1 Orange Pinch Salt and Pepper Dry Brine: 2 Tbs Honey 2 Tbs Soy Sauce Salt and Pepper Instructions: Delete All - Thaw the duck in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Day Before: - Trim the skin around the neck leaving a 1" flap, and remove the tips of the wings. - Remove the giblets and pat the duck dry with paper towels. - Slash the skin all the way through the fat layer without going through to the meat, in about 1" intervals to help the fat render out. - Brush with dry brine and season with salt and pepper on all sides. - Stuff the duck with quartered orange and onion. - Place on a metal cooling grate over a baking sheet and refrigerate overnight, uncovered. Cook Day: - Prepare smoker to cook at 300 - 325 degrees. - Glaze the duck, liberally. - Set High alarm to 157 degrees on the meat channel. - Set high alarm to 330 and low alarm to 295 on smoker channel. - Smoke for 2 1/2 hours. - Remove and rest duck for 20 min before slicing. - If the duck starts to get too dark, cover with foil.

title: Smoked Ham & Potato Soup
text: Smoked Ham & Potato Soup Smoked Ham & Potato Soup Ingredients Delete All 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil 1 1/2 cups chopped onion 3/4 cup chopped parsnips or carrots 3/4 cup chopped celery 1 clove garlic, minced 1 meaty ham bone from a ham, or a meaty ham shank (see recipe note) 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock 2 bay leaves 2 sprigs thyme 2 pounds Russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes 1 1/2 cups cubed ham (if using a ham bone), 3/4-inch dice 1/2 teaspoon ground pepper 1/4 cup whipping cream Salt to taste Instructions Delete All Heat olive oil in a large, thick-bottomed pot or Dutch oven on medium high heat. Add the onions, parsnips or carrots, celery, and sauté for 7 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a minute more. Add the ham bone or ham shank to the pot. Add 6 cups of stock. Add bay leaves and thyme. Bring to a boil, lower the heat to maintain a simmer. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes. Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 more minutes, until they are cooked through. Remove the ham bone or ham shank, bay leaves and thyme from the soup. Purée half of the soup so that some of the potatoes get puréed to give the soup body, and there are still whole chunks of potatoes for texture. If using a ham shank, cut away the meat and chop into 3/4-inch cubes. Add the chopped ham and black pepper to the soup. Stir in the cream, taste for salt and pepper. title: Smoked Hamburger
text: Smoked Hamburger Smoked Hamburger Serves 2–4 Ingredients Delete All 1 lb ground beef (preferably chuck with ~20% fat) Seasoning of choice (e.g., Canadian Steak or Cajun) Cheese (optional) Instructions Preheat smoker to 225°F. Season burgers with your choice of seasoning. Place burgers on a rack before putting them in the smoker. Smoke burgers for about 45 minutes, until internal temp reaches 135°F. Add cheese on top and smoke for an additional 15 minutes, until internal temp reaches 155°F.

title: Smoked Meatballs
text: Smoked Meatballs Smoked Meatballs Serves 6–8 Ingredients Delete All 2 lb ground beef (or 1 lb beef + 1 lb ground pork) 2 large eggs, whisked 1 medium red onion, diced small 1 carrot, diced small 1 red bell pepper, diced small 1 tbsp garlic, minced 1.5 tsp Italian seasoning, dried ½ tsp black pepper 1 tsp salt 24 oz pasta sauce (your choice) Instructions Preheat smoker to 225°F. In a large mixing bowl, combine ground meat, eggs, onion, carrot, red pepper, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Mix thoroughly. Form meatballs (~3” each) using a ¼ cup scoop or large spoon. Place on a rimmed sheet pan or cast iron skillet, leaving space between each. Smoke meatballs immediately or cover and refrigerate for up to 1 day before smoking. Place meatballs in the smoker on a rack. Smoke at 225°F for 1 hour. Preheat smoker to 325°F. Pour half of the pasta sauce into a large baking dish, place meatballs on top, then pour remaining sauce over them. Continue smoking meatballs in pasta sauce for about 45 minutes, until internal temp reaches 160°F. Serve when cool enough to enjoy. Perfect for sandwiches or pasta dishes.

title: Smoked Pork Loin Country Style Ribs
text: Smoked Pork Loin Country Style Ribs Smoked Pork Loin Country Style Ribs Ingredients Delete All Pork Loin Country Style Ribs Pork Magic BBQ Sauce Instructions Delete All ** Can be done 2 ways ** Smoke them for the entire 4 - 5 hours Smoke them for 2 hours then reverse sear them on the grill w/ BBQ Sauce Baste the ribs with Olive Oil and Pork Magic. title: Smoked Pork Loin w/ Sauerkraut and Apples
text: Smoked Pork Loin w/ Sauerkraut and Apples Smoked Pork Loin w/ Sauerkraut and Apples Ingredients Delete All 1 - 2 to 2 1/2 lbs Pork Loin Roast 1 Lb Bag Sauerkraut (last time I used a 2 LB bag) 2 Cooking Apples, Peeled, Cored, and Sliced (last time I used Golden Delicious Apples) 1 Sweet Onion, Thinly Sliced 1 Cup Dark Beer (last time I used Big Voodoo Daddy Dark Beer) 2 TBS Butter, melted 2 Bay Leaves 1/3 Cup Brown Sugar (last time I used a little more and was still not enough) Paul Predhomes Pork Magic Instructions Delete All The night before - trim the pork and season with Pork Magic. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Remove in the morning to bring pork to room temp. Pre - heat the smoker, with dry chips / chunks at 225 degrees for 15 min. Place the roast directly on the grill grates and smoke for 1 hour. Pre - heat the oven to 350 degrees. title: Smoked Pork Tenderloin
text: Smoked Pork Tenderloin Smoked Pork Tenderloin Ingredients: Delete All Pork: 1 - 1 1/2 pound whole pork tenderloin Handful of apple and pecan wood chunks Rub: 2 tablespoons brown sugar 2 tablespoons paprika 1 tablespoon salt 1 teaspoon onion powder 1/2 teaspoon black pepper 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder Barbecue Sauce: 1/2 cup ketchup 1/2 cup brown sugar 1/4 cup Worcestershire sauce 2 tablespoons white vinegar 1 teaspoon garlic powder 1 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon black pepper Instructions: Delete All - Preheat your smoker to 225°F. - Combine brown sugar, paprika, salt, onion powder, black pepper, and mustard powder in a bowl and mix with your fingers to break up any lumps. Generously apply the rub to all sides of the pork tenderloin. - Place the tenderloin in your smoker with 2 to 3 wood chunks on top of the hot coals. Cook until the deepest section of the pork tenderloin reaches an internal temperature of 110°F, or about 1 to 1 1/2 hours. - While the pork is cooking, combine all barbecue sauce ingredients in a saucepan and simmer for 10 minutes. - Once the tenderloin has reached its targeted temperature, brush it with barbecue sauce. - Preheat your grill for direct grilling at 500°F. - Transfer the pork tenderloin to the grill and cook until the internal temperature reaches 155°F, about 2 minutes per side. - Remove the tenderloin from the grill and let rest at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Smoked Potatoes
text: Smoked Potatoes Smoked Potatoes Ingredients: Delete All 1.5 lbs baby Yukon gold or baby red potatoes, quartered or 1 inch chunks 1 tablespoon avocado oil 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper 1/4 teaspoon ground oregano 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder 1/4 teaspoon onion powder 1/4 teaspoon marjoram Instructions: Delete All 1. Preheat grill to 225. 2. Place potatoes in a medium mixing bowl. Add oil, salt, pepper, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder and marjoram. Stir to coat the potatoes. 3. Create a foil boat and spray the bottom with non-stick or olive oil. Pour the potatoes inside. Place a dollop or two of butter (or ghee or plant butter) on top. 4. Place on the smoker and close the lid. Let smoke for 1.5 – 2 hours. 5. Increase smoker temp to 350 degrees (or stick them in the oven at this point). and let potatoes continue to cook for 20-30 minutes – or until they have reached your desired softness. 6. Remove from smoker and serve immediately. ** You can bake these as well, substitute rosemary, basil, parsley; add real garlic etc**

title: Smoked Prime Rib with Red Wine Sauce
text: Smoked Prime Rib with Red Wine Sauce Smoked Prime Rib with Red Wine Sauce Ingredients: Delete All Prime Rib: One 4-rib prime rib roast (6 to 8 pounds), untrimmed 1 cup Bobby Flay's Spice Rub for Pork and Beef, recipe follows Kosher salt Red Wine Steak Sauce: 2 tablespoons canola oil 8 cloves garlic, chopped 2 shallots, chopped 2 plum tomatoes, chopped 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons dry red wine 1 cup ketchup 1/4 cup golden raisins 2 tablespoons molasses 2 tablespoons brown sugar 1 heaping tablespoon horseradish 1 heaping tablespoon Dijon mustard 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce 1 teaspoon cayenne powder 1/2 teaspoon ground allspice Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper Splash red wine vinegar Bobby Flay's Spice Rub for Pork and Beef: 4 tablespoons ancho chile powder (or regular chili powder) 2 tablespoons ground coriander 2 tablespoons dry mustard 2 tablespoons Spanish paprika 2 tablespoons freshly ground black pepper 2 tablespoons kosher salt 1 tablespoon chile de arbol powder (or "Mexican Style Chile Powder) 1 tablespoon ground cumin 1 tablespoon dried oregano Directions: Delete All - Special equipment: Hickory wood chips, soaked in cold water for 2 hours - For the prime rib: Rub the prime rib with the spice rub, put in the refrigerator on a rack set over a baking sheet (uncovered) and let marinate for at least 4 hours and up to 8 hours. - For the red wine steak sauce: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and shallots and cook until soft, about 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, increase the heat to high and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the wine, ketchup, 1/2 cup water, raisins, molasses, brown sugar, horseradish, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire, cayenne, allspice and salt and pepper to taste and cook for 10 minutes longer. Add a splash of red wine vinegar, and taste for salt and pepper. Transfer to a blender and blend until smooth. Let cool to room temperature. - Prepare your grill using a kamado-style grill, kettle grill, bullet smoker or gas grill method for smoking. Remove the prime rib from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking and let sit at room temperature. Sprinkle well with salt and put the prime rib, fat-side up, on the grill grate. Maintaining a temperature of about 250 degrees F (if using a kettle grill or bullet smoker, replenish fire with unlit coals, as needed, to maintain temperature; see manufacturer's instructions), cook until an instant-read thermometer inserted in the center reads 130 degrees F, between 3 1/2 to 4 hours. During the last hour of cooking (at about 110 degrees F), begin brushing with some of the red wine steak sauce and stop adding chips to the smoker. Remove the prime rib from the grill, brush with more of the red wine steak sauce and let rest, loosely covered with foil, for 20 minutes before slicing. - Bobby Flay's Spice Rub for Pork and Beef: Combine all ingredients in a small bowl.

title: Smoked Pulled Pork Butt / Shoulder
text: Smoked Pulled Pork Butt / Shoulder Smoked Pulled Pork Butt / Shoulder Two Methods: Last Time & Next Time Ingredients — Last Time Delete All 4–6 lb bone-in pork shoulder roast (Boston Butt) 3 tbsp yellow mustard 1/4 cup BBQ Sweet Rub (Evernote) 1 tbsp BBQ Sweet Rub (Evernote) Instructions — Last Time Preheat smoker to 225°F. Remove roast from package; pat dry thoroughly. Coat entire pork shoulder with yellow mustard. Season all sides with the rub. Place pork fat-side up in the center of the smoker grate. Smoke until internal temp reaches 195–205°F (15–20 hours). Remove pork, wrap tightly in foil, and rest for 1 hour. Pull pork, discarding fat and gristle; sprinkle remaining rub and serve. To reheat: Add 2 tbsp water, cover, bake at 350°F for 30 min. Ingredients — Next Time For the Rub: 3 tbsp sea salt 2 tbsp black pepper 2 tbsp granulated garlic 2 tbsp granulated onion 2 tbsp paprika 2 tbsp cumin Spritzer / Sauce: 1 cup apple juice 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar 1/2 cup water For the Pork: 6–9 lb pork shoulder or butt, fat trimmed 4 tbsp yellow or Dijon mustard Instructions — Next Time Preheat smoker to 250°F. Rub mustard on all sides of pork. Season generously with rub. Smoke pork for 3 hours. Spritz pork every hour for the next 3 hours. At 165–170°F internal temp (~6–7 hours), double-wrap tightly in foil. Return to smoker bone-side up; cook to 200–205°F (2–4 hours). Rest 60 minutes in foil (inside cooler optional). Pull pork, discard large fat pieces, remove bone. Chef’s Notes Reheat at 325°F for 30 min with a little beef or chicken stock. Important: Ensure the top pork skin has split before wrapping.

title: Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict
text: Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict Smoked Salmon Eggs Benedict A delightful twist on the classic Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon and avocado. Ingredients: Delete All 2 English Muffins, Split 1 Large Avocado, Sliced 2 TBS Fresh Dill 1 tsp Capers Heirloom Tomatoes, for Serving 4 Large Eggs 1 TBS White Vinegar 3 oz Smoked Salmon For Hollandaise Sauce: 4 Egg Yolks 1 TBS Fresh Lemon Juice Salt and Black Pepper 1/2 Cup Butter, Melted Directions: Delete All - Prepare ingredients: thaw smoked salmon, slice avocado, chop fresh dill. - Prepare the Hollandaise Sauce: whisk egg yolks, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. - Slowly whisk in melted butter over simmering water until sauce thickens. - Toast the English Muffins. - Poach the eggs with a dash of vinegar in simmering water. - Assemble: layer muffin with avocado, smoked salmon, and poached egg. - Smother with Hollandaise Sauce, garnish with dill and capers. - If sauce is too thick, thin with hot water and whisk.

title: Snow Cream
text: Snow Cream Snow Cream A classic winter treat Ingredients Delete All Option 1 (Classic) 2 cups milk 2 tbsp vanilla ½ cup sugar 2 quarts clean, fresh snow Option 2 (Creamy) 1–3 cups clean, fresh snow ½ cup whipping cream 1 tbsp sugar 2–3 drops vanilla Instructions Collect fresh, clean snow in a large bowl. title: Soft Shell Crab on the Grill
text: Soft Shell Crab on the Grill Soft Shell Crab on the Grill Serves 3–6 Ingredients Delete All 6 soft-shell crabs 1/4 cup olive oil Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste Instructions Rinse crabs under cold running water and use a small brush if necessary to remove dirt from shells. Twist off and discard the apron. Fold back the pointed sides of the top shell to expose the gills; remove gills on both sides. Using kitchen scissors, cut across the front of the crab about 1/4 inch behind the eyes and mouth, and squeeze out the small sac behind the mouth. Preheat grill to medium-high heat with the lid down. Brush crabs with some olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place crabs on the grill, cover, and cook, turning every few minutes and basting with remaining olive oil, until orange and cooked through, 7–9 minutes depending on size. Remove from grill and serve hot.

title: Southern Baked Beans
text: Southern Baked Beans Southern Baked Beans Ingredients: 2 - 16 oz cans pork and beans 1 Large Onion - diced 3 Tbs Yellow Mustard 1/4 Cup Maple Syrup 1/4 Cup Light Brown Sugar 4 Tbs Ketchup 1 Tbs Lemon Juice 1/2 lb Bacon, cut into 1/2 inch pieces Instructions: Preheat oven to 350 F In a Dutch Oven (cast iron skillet with lid), combine all ingredients with bacon on top Bake covered for 45 - 60 minutes OR smoke uncovered for 3 - 4 hours

title: Speedy Ratatouille with Goat Cheese
text: Speedy Ratatouille with Goat Cheese Speedy Ratatouille with Goat Cheese Ingredients Delete All 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling 1 pound eggplant, peeled and cut into 1-inch dice 5 large garlic cloves, minced Salt and freshly ground black pepper 1 zucchini, cut into 1/2-inch dice 1 yellow squash, cut into 1/2-inch dice 1 large onion, cut into 1/2-inch dice 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice 2 pounds tomatoes, cored and finely chopped 1 cup loosely packed shredded basil leaves 1/2 teaspoon finely grated lemon zest 1/2 teaspoon fresh lemon juice 1/2 cup crumbled aged goat cheese Instructions Delete All In a large enameled cast-iron casserole or Dutch oven, heat 1/4 cup of the olive oil until shimmering. Add the eggplant and cook over moderately high heat, stirring occasionally, until almost tender, about 5 minutes. Add one-third of the garlic, season with salt and black pepper and cook for 1 minute. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the eggplant to a plate. Add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil to the casserole along with the zucchini and yellow squash and cook over moderate heat until lightly browned in spots, about 5 minutes. Add another one-third of the garlic, season with salt and black pepper and cook for 1 minute. Add the vegetables to the eggplant. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil to the casserole, along with the onion and bell pepper. Cook over moderate heat until softened, about 7 minutes. Add the remaining garlic, season with salt and black pepper and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, two-thirds of the basil and the reserved vegetables and cook over moderate heat until the tomatoes have broken down and the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes. Stir in the remaining basil along with the lemon zest and juice. Transfer to bowls and sprinkle with the goat cheese. Drizzle with olive oil and serve. title: Spicy Cajun Shrimp & Andouille Sweet Potato Boats
text: Spicy Cajun Shrimp & Andouille Sweet Potato Boats Spicy Cajun Shrimp & Andouille Sweet Potato Boats Meal Prep Version – 4 Lunches (2 stuffed sweet potatoes, 4 servings) Ingredients Delete All 2 medium sweet potatoes ½ lb raw shrimp, peeled, deveined, chopped 3 oz andouille sausage, diced 1–2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp olive oil ½ tbsp butter 1 tsp Cajun seasoning Pinch–⅛ tsp cayenne pepper 1½ tbsp whipped cream cheese 1–1½ tbsp whole milk Greek yogurt Kosher salt & black pepper Olive oil (for potato skins) Instructions Preheat oven to 425°F. Wash and dry sweet potatoes. Rub skins with olive oil and salt. Bake 45–55 min until fork tender. Slice in half, scoop out ⅓–½ of flesh, brush lightly with olive oil. Return to oven 5–8 min for sturdier boats. Heat olive oil & butter in skillet over medium heat. Add garlic 30 sec. Add sausage 2–3 min. Add shrimp & Cajun seasoning, cook until opaque (1–2 min). Stir in cream cheese, Greek yogurt, cayenne, salt & pepper. Optional: mash a spoonful of sweet potato for stability. Spoon mixture into sweet potato halves. Bake 400–425°F for 8–10 min to lightly set. Cool slightly before portioning. Store in airtight containers up to 4 days. Reheat gently to avoid overcooking shrimp.

title: Spinach and Bacon Pizza
text: Spinach and Bacon Pizza Spinach and Bacon Pizza Ingredients: Delete All 5-6 tbsp marinara or pizza sauce 6 oz fresh mozzarella, sliced (more if desired) 1 bag (9 ounces) fresh spinach leaves 6 slices bacon, cooked and chopped Roma tomato (optional) Sautéed mushrooms (optional) Instructions: Delete All 1. Heat grill to around 500° F. 2. Chop and cook the bacon. 3. Grill the pizza crust on the ‘finished side’ for 2 - 3 min. Remove and flip the pizza crust. 4. As the grill is heating up, heat a skillet over medium. Add the fresh spinach leaves and allow them to wilt, stirring occasionally for about 5 minutes. When the leaves have wilted, remove from heat and drain the leaves on a paper towel. When the leaves have cooled, wring them through another towel to remove any excess moisture. Set aside. 5. On the turned over pizza crust, lightly spread the marinara sauce then top with the sliced mozzarella and spinach leaves. Sprinkle the cooked chopped bacon on top. When this is complete, transfer the pizza back on to the grill. Close the grill lid and cook for an additional 4 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and golden. 6. title: Spinach, Artichoke and Brie Crepes w/ Sweet Honey Sauce
text: Spinach, Artichoke and Brie Crepes w/ Sweet Honey Sauce Spinach, Artichoke and Brie Crepes w/ Sweet Honey Sauce Ingredients Delete All WHOLE WHEAT CREPES: 2 Large Eggs 3/4 Cup Milk 1 Cup Flour 3 TBS Butter, Melted 1/4 tsp Salt 1/4 Cup Water FILLING: 2 TBS Olive Oil 2 Cloves Garlic, Minced 1/4 tsp Salt 1/2 tsp Pepper 1/2 tsp Crushed Red Pepper ( optional ) 1 (8 oz) bag Fresh Spinach 1 (12 oz ) Jar Marinated Artichoke Hearts, Drained and Chopped 1/4 Cup Parmesan Cheese Finely Grated 1 ( 8 oz ) Brie Wheel cut into Slices ** Add some roasted chopped chicken for some protein ** SWEET HONEY SAUCE: 1/4 Cup Olive Oil 3 TBS Honey 1/4 Cup Fresh Parsley, Chopped Instructions Delete All Start by making the crepes. Add all of the ingredients to a bowl and use an immersion blender to blend until smooth. Set aside for 30 min to allow the air bubbles to subside. Heat large pan, add cooking spray to coat. Pour 1/3 Cup of batter into the center of the pan and swirl to spread evenly. Cook for 30 sec. and flip. Cook for another 10 sec. and remove to cool. Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add 1 TBS of olive oil and garlic. Add the salt, pepper and crushed red pepper, if using, and cook for 2 min. Stir in Spinach and artichokes, cooking 5 - 6 minutes until spinach is fully wilted. Reduce heat to low and stir in parmesan cheese, then turn off heat. Whisk together the olive oil and honey. Place in a small sauce pot and worm through. Keep warm until ready to use. Wipe the skillet clean and heat over medium - low heat. Law a few slices of brie on one quarter of the crepe (basically make a triangle). Layer on the spinach and artichoke filling, chicken and another layer of brie. Fold over the bottom of the crepe and over again to make a triangle. Cook for 2 - 3 min and flip and cook for another 2 - 3 min or until the brie is melty and gooey. Remove the honey sauce from the heat and stir in the chopped parsley. Drizzle the crepe with the warm honey sauce and dig in! Image - add later --> Image - add later -->

text: Street Waffles Recipe Street Waffles Ingredients: Delete All 4 egg yolks 3/4 cup milk 2 tsp vanilla extract 1/3 cup butter, melted 3/4 cup sugar 1 cup + 2 Tbsp flour 1 1/2 tsp baking powder Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg 1/8 tsp salt 6 egg whites, beaten to stiff peaks Vegetable oil (for cooking) Optional toppings: Fresh fruit, honey, syrup, powdered sugar, whipped cream Instructions: Delete All 1. Eggplant: - Grill eggplant for 4 min over direct medium heat. - Turn them over, top each slice with about 1 tsp freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, continue to grill until the cheese is melted, about 4 min.

title: Tonkotsu Ramen
text: Tonkotsu Ramen Tonkotsu Ramen Ingredients Delete All Tonkotsu Ramen: 8 Cups Tonkotsu Pork Broth (See Recipe) 12 oz Good Quality Dried Ramen Noodles 4 Large or Extra Large Eggs 2 - 3 oz Enoki or other Mushrooms ( I used oyster last time) Thinly Sliced Green Onions Chashu Pork Belly 2 lb Pork Belly - rolled and tied 1/4 Cup Soy Sauce 1/2 Cup Sake 1/2 Cup Mirin 1/4 Cup Sugar 2 - 3 Cloves Garlic - left whole 2 Green Onions - coursely chopped Soy Bacon Tare 2 Slices Bacon 1/4 Cup Soy Sauce 2 Tbs Mirin 2 Tbs Sake 4 Tbs Shiro Miso Miso Tare 1/2 Cup Shiro Miso 1/4 Cup Sake 1/4 Cup Mirin Pinch Shichimi Togarashi - a Japanese Spice (optional) 1 - 2 tps Kosher Salt - depending on how salty you like your ramen Instructions Delete All Chashu Pork Belly Combine soy, sake, mirin, sugar, garlic and green onions in a zip lock bag big enough to hold the pork belly. Stick a straw in the bag and seal the ziplock bag up against it. Suck out as much of the air as you can and seal Sous vide the pork for 10 - 11 hours at 170 degrees Remove pork from the bag, Discard the bag and marinade. Let the chashu pork belly cool completely. Slice across the chashu pork (so you get bacon like slices) - into 8 - 12 slices about 1/8 to 3/16 inches thick. Reserve. You won't need all of the pork for 4 servings. Soy Bacon Tare Combine all the ingredients in a small sauce pan. Simmer at the lowest setting for about an hour. Top up with a bit of chicken stock if needed. Remove the bacon Miso Tare Combine all ingredients in a small sauce pan and simmer at the lowest setting for about 5 minutes Medium Boiled Eggs Bring enough water to cover the eggs to a boil. Prick the egg. Boil large eggs for 6 min & 30 seconds. Submerge the eggs in ice water to chill. Peel and cut in half right before you serve the ramen Assemble the Tonkotsu Ramen Boil the ramen noodles in plenty of water as directed, usually 4 min. You don't need to salt the water. Cook the mushrooms alongside the noodles - you just want them softened Gently fry the chashu pork in a non - stick skillet until lightly browned Place 1/4 of the tare in the bottom of 4 bowls Ladle in 1/2 cup of the tonkotsu broth into each of the bowls and stir to mix. Add the noodles. Pour in another 1 1/2 cups of broth per bowl Top with the egg, mushrooms, pork and green onions NOTES Use only 1 of the tare recipes or use your own. If you use the miso tare, you can salt your broth directly. That is easier than guessing how salty you want your tare. If you aren't up for making chashu pork you can substitute roasted pork shoulder. It would be an awesome us of a leftover pork roast. --> Image - add later --> Image - add later

title: Tonkotsu Ramen Broth
text: Tonkotsu Ramen Broth Tonkotsu Ramen Broth Ingredients Delete All 6 Lbs pork neck bones 4 oz white mushrooms sliced 1 Onion peeled and halved. Instructions Delete All Place the pork bones in a large stock pot and cover with cold water Bring to a rolling boil over medium high heat. A huge mess of scum will form. Remove from heat. Dump the water carefully rinse the bones under cold running water. Return the bones to the stock pot. Cover the bones with cold water and bring to a rolling boil. Add the mushrooms and onion and maintain a rolling boil for 12 hours, replenishing the water along the way. You want to keep the bones under the water the whole time. It's best to cover the pot for this or you'll be adding water every 30 min. After 12 hours, remove the stock from the heat and cool slightly. Remove the bones and strain the stock. The stock will keep in the refrigerator for 2 - 3 days or frozen The broth is flavored by the tare of your choice. Image - add later --> Image - add later -->

title: Tortilla Pinwheels

Cream Cheese, Softened 1 Can (4 oz) Diced Green Chilis 1 Can (4 oz) Chopped Black Olives 1 Cup Cheddar Cheese, Grated 1/2 Cup Green Onions Garlic Powder to Taste Flour Tortillas Salsa for Dip Instructions: Delete All 1. title: Tuna and Avocado Tartare
text: Tuna and Avocado Tartare Tuna and Avocado Tartare Ingredients: Delete All 2 tsp tan or black sesame seeds (toast the tan, do not toast the black) 1/2 small bunch of chives, finely chopped (or green onions) 1 tbsp soy sauce (reduce to a splash) Juice of 1 lime, divided 1/4 tsp sesame oil 14 oz sushi-grade tuna, cut into small cubes Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper (optional) 1 large avocado, peeled, pitted, and cubed Instructions: Delete All 1. Toast tan sesame seeds in a small skillet over low heat until golden. Let cool. 2. Mix chives, soy sauce, half the lime juice, and sesame oil in a medium bowl. Add the tuna, season with salt and pepper, and toss. 3. In another bowl, gently fold in the avocado with the remaining lime juice. 4. Divide the tuna mixture into four plates. Form a small mound in the center. 5. Spoon avocado on top, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve immediately. Notes: Use a 2-3 inch pastry ring to mold the tuna and avocado neatly on the plate. Serve with pita chips or tortillas for a delicious appetizer. Pair with an arugula salad with ginger dressing for a complete meal.

title: Tuna Steak with Mango and Cucumber Salsa
text: Tuna Steak with Mango and Cucumber Salsa Tuna Steak with Mango and Cucumber Salsa Ingredients: Delete All 1 Small Mango, Peeled and Finely Diced 1 Small Red Onion, Finely Diced 1/2 Cucumber, Diced 1/2 Small Bunch of Cilantro, roughly chopped 1/2 Small Bunch Basil, roughly chopped 2 1/2 TBS unsalted peanuts, roughly chopped (optional) 1 Red Chile, seeded and finely chopped (or Poblano) 2 tsp Fish Sauce (find a replacement) Juice of 2 Limes Olive Oil for Drizzling 2 Tuna Steaks Salt and freshly ground pepper 2 Little Gem Lettuce, leaves separated and washed Instructions: Delete All - Mix the diced mango with the onion, cucumber, cilantro, basil, peanuts, and red chile. Pour in the fish sauce and lime juice and mix everything together. Taste and adjust the seasoning as necessary. - Drizzle a little olive oil over the tuna steaks and rub it into both sides of the fish. Season with salt and pepper. - Place a heavy-bottomed nonstick skillet (cast iron) over high heat. When hot, carefully put the fish into the pan and cook for 50 seconds on each side. Remove the fish from the pan and leave to rest for a couple of minutes. - Gently toss the lettuce leaves through the salsa and pile up onto two plates. Slice the tuna steaks thickly, then place them on top of the leaves and serve.

title: Turkey & Veggie Bake
text: Turkey & Veggie Bake Turkey & Veggie Bake Ingredients: Delete All 2 Cups Fresh Mushrooms - sliced 3/4 Cup Red or Yellow Pepper, Chopped 1/2 Cup Onion, Chopped 2 Cloves Garlic, Minced 2 TBS Margarine or Veg Oil Spread 1/4 Cup Flour 3/4 tsp Salt 1/2 tsp dried thyme 1/4 tsp black pepper 2 Cups fat-free Milk 1 - 10 oz package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained 2 Cups Cooked brown or white rice 2 Cups Cooked Turkey or Chicken 1/2 Cup Finely Shredded Parm Cheese Instructions: Delete All - In a 12 in skillet cook and stir mushrooms, sweet peppers, onion and garlic in hot butter or oil over medium heat until tender. - Stir in flour, salt, thyme, and black pepper. Slowly stir in milk; cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Stir in spinach, rice, turkey and 1/4 Cup of the Parm cheese. - Spoon mixture into a 2-quart rectangular baking dish. Sprinkle with remaining Parm Cheese. Bake, covered, in a 350 degrees F oven for 20 min. Uncover and bake about 10 min more or until heated through. Let stand 15 min before serving.

title: Turkey Chili
text: Turkey Chili Turkey Chili Ingredients: Turkey: Delete All 2 lb Ground Turkey 1 1/2 tsp Cumin 1 1/2 tsp Coriander 1 1/2 tsp Worcestershire Sauce Salt & Pepper Chili: 1 Green Pepper, Chopped 1 Large Onion, Chopped 2 Celery Stalks, Chopped 2 TBS Worcestershire Sauce 2 TBS Franks or Tabasco Sauce (wait until done and add then) 2 TBS Brown Sugar 1 Large Can Diced Tomatoes 1 Large Can Chili Hot Beans (or mild) 1/2 - 1 Bottle of Killian's or other dark beer 2 Cap Fulls of Bourbon 1 Small Can Stewed Tomatoes (Last time I added "Mexican Style") Instructions: Delete All - Sauté turkey with Worcestershire, cumin, coriander, salt and pepper until cooked through. - In a large pot, add EVOO and butter and sauté green pepper, onion, celery. - Add remaining ingredients, bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and simmer for at least an hour.

title: Turkey Sausage Sauté with Cabbage and Scallions

title: Turkey Tortellini Toss
text: Turkey Tortellini Toss Turkey Tortellini Toss Ingredients: Delete All 1 Package Fresh 3 Cheese Tortellini 1 LB Ground Turkey 2 Medium Zucchini, halved lengthwise and sliced 2 Garlic Cloves, Minced 1 1/2 Cups Cherry Tomatoes, Halved 1 tsp Dried Oregano 1/4 tsp Salt 1/4 tsp Crushed Red Pepper Flakes 1 Cup Shredded Asiago Cheese, Divided 1 Tbs Olive Oil Instructions: Delete All - Cook Tortellini according to instructions. - Meanwhile, in a large skillet, cook turkey, zucchini, garlic over medium heat, 7 - 9 min or until turkey is no longer pink, breaking up turkey into crumbles. - Drain. Add tomatoes, oregano, salt, pepper and cook 2 minutes longer. Stir in 3/4 Cup Cheese. - Add tortellini to skillet and toss to combine. Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with remaining cheese.

title: Turkey with Cilantro Pesto
text: Turkey with Cilantro Pesto Turkey with Cilantro Pesto Serves 4 Ingredients: Delete All 1 Lb Turkey Steaks / Chop, cut into 2-inch cubes 2 zucchini, thickly sliced 1 Red and 1 Yellow bell pepper, cut into 2-inch squares 8 Cherry Tomatoes 8 Pearl Onions, peeled Marinade: 6 Tbs Olive Oil 3 Tbs dry White Wine 1 tsp green peppercorns, crushed (can substitute some capers and black pepper) 2 Tbs chopped fresh cilantro Salt Cilantro Pesto: 4 Tbs chopped fresh cilantro 1 Tbs chopped fresh parsley 1 garlic clove 1/2 cup pine nuts 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 6 Tbs EVOO Juice of 1 lemon Directions: Delete All - To make the marinade, mix the olive oil, wine, peppercorns and cilantro together in a measuring cup and season to taste with salt. - Pour the mixture over the turkey in a Ziploc bag, seal and marinate for 2 hours. - To make the Pesto, put the Cilantro and Parsley into a food processor and process until finely chopped. - Add the garlic and pine nuts and pulse until chopped. - Add the Parmesan, EVOO, and lemon juice and process briefly to mix. - Transfer to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate until required. - Drain the turkey, reserving the marinade. - Thread the turkey, zucchini slices, bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, and onions onto metal or pre-soaked wooden skewers. - Cook over medium-hot heat, turning and brushing frequently with the marinade, for 10 minutes, until cooked through.

title: Tuscan vegetable pasta soup
text: Tuscan vegetable pasta soup Tuscan vegetable pasta soup Ingredients Delete All Serves: 6 - 8 Prep Time: 10 Min | Cook Time: 20 Min 2 TBS EVOO 4 Cloves Garlic, minced 1 Medium Yellow Onion, diced 1/2 Cup Carrot, chopped 1/2 Cup Celery, chopped 1 Medium Zucchini, sliced and quartered 1 - 15 oz Can Diced Tomatoes 6 Cups low sodium Vegetable Stock 2 Tbs Tomato Paste 6 - 8 oz Whole Wheat Pasta 1 - 15 oz Can White Beans 2 Large Handfuls Baby Spinach 6 Dorot Basil Cubes or 6 tsp Minced Basil Salt and Pepper, to Taste Fresh Chopped Parsley, for garnish Instructions Delete All Drizzle olive oil in a large pot and add in diced onion and garlic. title: Ultimate Barbecued Chicken
text: Ultimate Barbecued Chicken Ultimate Barbecued Chicken Brine: Delete All 2 Quarts water 2 Tbs kosher salt 1/4 Cup brown sugar 2 garlic cloves, smashed 4 Sprigs fresh thyme 6 Chicken Legs and Thighs, still connected, bone in, skin on, about 10 oz Ultimate Barbecue Sauce: 1 Slice Bacon 1 Bunch fresh thyme EVOO 1/2 Onion, chopped 2 Garlic cloves, chopped 2 Cups ketchup 1/4 Cup brown sugar 1/4 Cup molasses 2 Tbs red or white wine vinegar 1 Tbs dry mustard 1 tsp ground cumin 1 tsp paprika Freshly ground black pepper Instructions: Delete All - For the brine, in a mixing bowl combine the water, salt, sugar, garlic, and thyme. - Transfer the brine to a 2-gallon sized re-sealable plastic bag. Add the chicken, close the bag and refrigerate 2 hours to allow the salt and seasonings to penetrate the chicken. - Meanwhile, make the sauce. Wrap the bacon around the bunch of thyme and tie with kitchen twine so you have a nice bundle. - Heat 2 Tbs of oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the thyme and cook slowly 3 to 4 min. to render the bacon fat and give the sauce a nice smoky taste. - Add the onion and garlic and cook slowly without coloring for 5 min. Add the remaining ingredients, give the sauce a stir, and turn the heat down to low. - Cook slowly for 20 min. to meld the flavors. Once the sauce is done cooking, remove about 1 1/2 Cups of the sauce and reserve for serving alongside the chicken at the table. The rest of the barbecue sauce will be used for basting the legs. - Preheat outer burners of the grill to medium heat. - Arrange the chicken pieces on the preheated grill and cook, turn once mid-way, and cook for a total of 10 min. - Transfer the chicken to a double-foil base on the indirect heat section of the grill. Cook the chicken for 15 min. - Brush liberally, coating every inch of the legs with the barbecue sauce and then cook for 25 - 30 more min, basting the chicken for a second time halfway through, serve with extra sauce.

title: Very Hot Cajun Sauce for Beef
text: Very Hot Cajun Sauce for Beef Very Hot Cajun Sauce for Beef Ingredients: Delete All 3/4 cup chopped onions 1/2 cup chopped green bell peppers 1/4 cup chopped celery 1/4 cup vegetable oil 1/4 cup plus 1 Tbs all purpose flour 3/4 tsp cayenne pepper 1/2 tsp white pepper 1/2 tsp black pepper 2 Bay leaves 1/4 cup minced jalapeño peppers 1 tsp minced garlic 3 cups Beef Stock Instructions: Delete All - Combine the onions, bell peppers, and celery in a small bowl and set aside while you start the roux. This is a Light Brown Roux so heat the oil to only 250°F. - In a heavy 2-quart saucepan, heat the oil over medium-low heat to about 250°F. With a metal whisk, whisk in the flour a little at a time until smooth. Continue cooking, whisking constantly, until the roux is light brown, about 2 to 3 minutes. Be careful not to let the roux scorch or splash on your skin. - Remove from heat and with a spoon immediately stir in the vegetable mixture and the red, white, and black peppers; return pan to high heat and cook about 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Add the bay leaves, jalapeño peppers, and garlic, stirring well. Continue cooking about 2 minutes, stirring constantly. (We’re cooking the seasonings and vegetables in the light roux and the mixture should, therefore, be pasty.) Remove from heat. - In a separate 2-quart saucepan, bring the stock to a boil. Add the roux mixture by spoonfuls to the boiling stock, stirring until dissolved between each addition. Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until the sauce reduces to 3 1/2 cups, about 15 minutes. Skim any oil from the top and serve immediately.

title: Zucchini and Tomato Ragu
text: Zucchini and Tomato Ragu Zucchini and Tomato Ragu Ingredients: Delete All 6 TBS EVOO 1 Onion, Roughly Chopped 2 Garlic Cloves, Lightly Crushed 1 Medium Zucchini, Sliced 1 Medium Squash, Sliced 1 Tomato, Chopped (1 Cup) 1/2 Cup Mozz Cheese, Torn or Small Balls 1/4 Cup Parsley, Roughly Chopped 1/4 Cup Basil Leaves, Torn Kosher Salt, Pepper Instructions: Delete All - Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring often, until the onion is translucent, 8 - 10 min. - Add the zucchini and squash, season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the zucchini and squash turn golden brown, about 2 min. - Stir in the tomatoes and cook until they have just begun to soften and the zucchini and squash are al dente, about 2 min. Serve topped with the Mozz, Parsley and Basil.

title: Zucchini Lasagna Rolls
text: Zucchini Lasagna Rolls Zucchini Lasagna Rolls Ingredients: Delete All 3 Large Zucchini, trimmed (about 4 lbs) 4 TBS EVOO 1/4 tsp Salt 2 Cups Crushed Tomatoes 1 tsp Italian Seasoning 4 tsp minced Garlic 1/4 Crushed Red Pepper 2 1/2 Cups Ricotta Cheese 1/4 Cup Grated Parm Cheese 1/2 tsp Ground Pepper 1/4 Cup Chopped Almonds Instructions: Delete All - Position racks in the middle and upper third of oven; preheat to 425°F. Coat 2 rimmed baking sheets with cooking spray. - Slice each zucchini lengthwise into 1/4 to 1/8 inch thick strips. Discard any small or misshapen pieces. You should have about 24 strips. Brush the strips with 3 TBS oil and sprinkle with 1/4 tsp salt. Place on the prepared baking sheets. Roast until softened, 20 - 25 min, set aside and cool slightly. - Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees. - Combine tomatoes, Italian Seasoning, 2 tsp garlic and crushed red pepper in a large bowl. Spread mixture in a 9 x 13 inch baking dish. Combine Ricotta, Parmesan, pepper and 1 tsp garlic in a med. bowl. - When Zucchini is cool enough to handle, spread a generous TBS of the ricotta mixture on each slice. Roll up the slices and place them in the baking dish seam-side down. Bake until hot, 25 - 30 min. - Meanwhile, place almonds, the remaining 1 tsp garlic and the remaining pinch of salt in a mini food processor. Process until ground to a coarse meal. Heat the remaining 1 TBS oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the almond mixture and cook, stirring frequently until lightly browned and fragrant, 1 - 2 min.

title: Zucchini Sticks
text: Zucchini Sticks Zucchini Sticks Ingredients: Delete All 3 Zucchini 1/2 cup whole wheat bread crumbs 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese Dash of Veggie Magic 2 eggs Instructions: Delete All 1. Preheat oven to 425°F. 2. Mix bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and Veggie Magic in a shallow dish. 3. Whisk eggs in another shallow dish. 4. Cut off zucchini ends and cut them in half lengthwise. 5. Cut the zucchini halves into 1-inch sticks. 6. Soak zucchini sticks in the egg wash, then coat them in the bread crumb mixture. 7. Place the coated zucchini sticks onto a foil-lined, oiled sheet pan. 8. Bake for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway through the cooking time.
